title: Father Divine, This Deadening Power Control
description: Father Divine, This Deadening Power Control in Tonic Solfa to EVENTIDE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Joseph Tuckerman wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 514, “My Heaven in Thee”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Tens (10.10.10.10) (10.10.10.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to EVENTIDE; any other Tens (10.10.10.10) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther di-vine, this dead-ening power con-trol, Which to the sens-es binds th'im-mor-tal soul; O break this bon-dage, Lord! I would be free, And in my soul would find my heaven, in Thee.

lines: Father divine, this deadening power control,
Which to the senses binds the immortal soul;
O break this bondage, Lord! I would be free,
And in my soul would find my heaven, in Thee.
My heaven in Thee! O God, no other heaven
To the immortal soul can e'er be given;
O, let Thy kingdom now within me come,
And as above, so here, Thy will be done!
My heaven in Thee, O Father, let me find —
My heaven in Thee, within a heart resigned;
No more, of heaven and bliss, my soul, despair,
For where my God is found, my heaven is there.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Joseph Tuckerman died in 1840.
credits: Words by Joseph Tuckerman (1778–1840), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to EVENTIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
